21 A wire has both elastic and plastic properties. When it is slowly loaded, its extension varies with
load as shown by line OXY. The removal of the load is represented by line YZ. This creates areas
P, Q and R on the graph.
X
Y
load

Q
R

Which area represents the maximum elastic potential energy stored in the wire?
A
P
B
Q
C
Q + R
D
R

hints: Look at the unloading line YZ on the load against extension graph: it returns to Z on the extension axis, not to O, so OZ is permanent plastic extension.
Remember that work done is the area under the load-extension curve, so the total work put in is the area under OXY and the work given back is the area under YZ.
Ask which labelled area lies directly under YZ down to the extension axis, because that recovered work must come from the elastic potential energy stored at point Y.
walkthrough: Identify the process: the wire is loaded along OXY to maximum load and extension at Y, then unloaded along YZ to zero load but non-zero extension at Z.
State the energy rule: for a load $F$ and small extension $dx$, work is $dW = F dx$, so work is the area under the load against extension curve.
Find total work in: the area between OXY and the extension axis is $Q + R$, so this is all the energy supplied during loading.
Find work out: on unloading the wire contracts from Y back to Z, so the recovered work is the area between YZ and the extension axis, which is $R$.

Link to storage: the recovered work can only come from elastic potential energy stored at Y, while the difference $Q$ is dissipated by plastic behaviour, so the maximum stored elastic energy is $R$. This is option D.

A.explanation: P is the area to the left of the loading line OXY, not the area under a load-extension line, so it does not represent $work = load \times extension$.

B.explanation: Q is the loop area between loading OXY and unloading YZ, so it represents net work lost as heat and plastic deformation, not recoverable energy.

C.explanation: Q + R is the area under the loading curve OXY to the extension axis, so it is the total work done on the wire including energy that is lost.

D.explanation: R is the area under the unloading line YZ to the extension axis, so it is the work recovered on contraction and equals the maximum elastic energy stored at Y.
